main_text.p: mori explicando sufficiant, liceat tamen quæ affert, AlSbarestanius apponere, في كانت العرب جاهليتها يحرمون اشياء نزل القران بتحريمها كانوا لا ينكحون الامهات ولا البنات ولا الاخوات ولا العمات وكان اقبح ما يصنعون ان يجمع الرجل بين الاختين او يخلف على امراة ابيه وكانوا يسمون من فعل ذلك الضيزن &c. Pro vetitis habuerunt Arabes ignorantiæ suæ temporibus aliqua, quæ postea vetuit eAl. Koranus; abstinere, siquidem a matribus, & à filiabus, & à marterteris & amitis, turpissimum autem eorum quæ faciebant hoc erat, quod vir duas sorores duceret & Patris sui uxorem velut successor assumeret, quod qui faceret appellabatur{*} AlDaizan, quo nomine infectatus est (inquit) Aus Ebn Hajar [Poëta] quosdam è tribu BaniKais, quorum tres, ex ordine, patris sui uxorem duxerant. وكان الرجل من العرب اذا مات عن المراة او طلقها قام اكبر بنيه فان كان لة فيها حاجة طرح ثوبة عليها وان لم يكن حاجة يزوجها بعض اخوته بمهر جديد Mos autem erat apud Arabes, ut cum ab uxore, morte aut repudio, separaretur aliquis, filiorum ipsius natu maximus, si eâ opus haberet, vestem suam ei injiceret, quod si ille opus ea non haberet, duceret ipsa è fratribus aliquò dotis nova interventu. Addi his possent ejusdem farinæ multa, sed è jam dictis & quales invenerit Arabes suos Mohammedes, & quales reliquerit, satis patere arbitror.Quod etiam Idoli nomen erat, AlIaoh. [?] & Kamus.

page.notes: Marginal note beside "appellabatur" is marked with an asterisk in the text. The name "AlIaoh" in the note is doubtful, the scan is small. "vetuit eAl. Koranus" is printed with the run-on "eAl." and may be "ei Al-Koranus"; kept as printed. The Arabic is transcribed letter by letter from a small scan. Words marked as doubtful in the Arabic are uncertain, and the Arabic line ends are approximate. The catchword "Quòd" is at the lower right and is not repeated in the text. Long s has been changed to plain s throughout.
